claim: Guided developmental labels preserve the sender-to-receiver topographic relation better than an exact receptor-label shuffle while keeping connection count and effective rank fixed.
design: matched-seed control
controls: Exact receptor-label shuffle with the same somata, dendrites, growth grammar, receptor/ligand multisets and seeded growth-noise generator
Chemoaffinity-disabled random walk
Zero-chemoaffinity regression proving label shuffling does not shift the growth-noise generator
limitations: Synthetic developmental world rather than biological neurodevelopment
Shows a developed relation and wiring effect, not a general computational advantage

claim: With identical passive dendritic operators, development changes only where input enters the physical basis; the resulting modal and transfer effect is sparse rather than broad.
design: matched-seed physical control
controls: Guided and shuffled arms use identical cable geometry, capacitance, conductance, system matrices and generalized eigenvalues
Only the developed input address can differ
limitations: Only 4 of 16 seeds place the guided input at a physically different relative dendritic port
Paired medians for visibility, purification time and soma transfer are essentially zero

claim: A morphology-only passive cable compiler plus a causal three-site nonlinear closure reproduces the standardized soma response across released morphologies without fitting the target cell.
design: cross-cell reference-model comparison

metrics.name: cells at or below 10% soma NRMSE

controls: 24 cells × 3 deterministic apical branches × 4 timing programs
Graph-current oracle comparison
Failed global waveform Picard arm retained as a numerical-architecture negative control
limitations: One retained rat L6 IPC outlier has 11.2% cell-median soma error
Accuracy validates this compiled numerical organization; it does not establish novelty of differentiable neuron simulation

claim: The tested phase multiplier changes fractal morphology beyond ordinary seed variation.
design: matched-seed null test
controls: Matched closed-loop versus no-write runs
Independent scale-free morphology check
limitations: The null narrows the morphology claim; it does not invalidate the field-generated interface or conservative operator machinery

claim: Keeping hidden world computation resident and applying relevance later causes the observed switch/readiness advantage over an equal-state generic recurrent baseline.
design: equal-state baseline comparison with destructive controls

metrics.name: median first query after rapid switch MSE

controls: Four recurrent state scalars in both models
28 learned route parameters in both models
Matched training episodes, optimizer updates and publication opportunities
Destructive relevance-leak and dense-recurrence variants
limitations: The generic baseline also fits the sparse training queries substantially worse
Training quality therefore confounds attribution of the readiness gap to architecture alone

claim: Actively choosing measurement addresses can identify a hidden law from scalar observations more reliably than fixed or random addressing in the registered finite-law world.
design: active-sensing identification with post-gate seed audit
controls: Fixed-address observer
Random moving address observer
Fixed-scale active observer, which also reached 100% and therefore attacks the multiscale interpretation
replication: 10-seed post-gate audit after the original 192/192 active trials
limitations: The law family and initial field are known
The active mechanism replicated, but the originally demanded >=0.20 margin over random passed only 5/10 seeds
The result supports active address selection, not a unique requirement for multiscale sensing

claim: Addressed dendritic stimulation removes the algebraic ambiguity of fixed soma observation, but the resulting full-rank code is not fully identifiable at the locked 1 uV soma-noise level.
design: real-morphology observability test with noise audit
controls: Fixed address with varying scale
Random multiscale probe sets
Point-only active probes
Flattened-radius morphology control
replication: 10 post-result noise seeds plus a noise sweep
limitations: Uses a passive graph model of one released human morphology rather than a population of cells
Full algebraic rank does not imply practical identifiability under realistic amplitude noise
Multiscale stimulation is not necessary because active point probes also reach full rank

claim: A known write can distinguish states that passive reading cannot when the write operator itself depends on the hidden state.
design: constructed observability/controllability mechanism test
controls: Two hidden states with the same row-space component and different measurement-nullspace components
Constant write Jacobian J negative control
limitations: The state-dependent writer is a synthetic tanh-gated construction
The result establishes existence of the mechanism, not its prevalence or usefulness in real decoders

claim: Coprime box-grid stacks beat the best single box grid by at least 0.02 capture at matched probe budget.
design: registered matched-budget attacker
controls: Best single grid at each matched budget rather than only a redundant dyadic pyramid
Five probe budgets from 64 through 512
limitations: The negative result narrows the earlier incommensurate-grid rank story; it does not erase the rank gain over stacked redundant dyadic sets

claim: Designed grouped rollback interventions plus one scalar KPI can localize a sparse set of harmful changes much more efficiently than equal-budget random individual rollback.
design: frozen practical regression-localization benchmark
controls: Equal-budget random individual rollback
Exhaustive individual rollback
Shuffled pulse address
Permutation-calibrated screen plus direct confirmations
limitations: Requires safe reversible candidate rollbacks
Assumes sparse faults and approximately additive grouped effects
Not a replacement for logs or exhaustive tests when those are cheap

claim: Under a valid local repair primitive, adaptive scalar-only interventions can localize scarce useful writes substantially better than equal-budget random probing.
design: paired scalar-only fault assay

metrics.name: mean damage recovered
metrics.comparison: adaptive pulse search vs equal-budget random probing

metrics.name: paired trials where adaptive beat random

controls: Equal-budget random probing
Exhaustive 128-tile scan
Known bilateral local repair primitive
limitations: Sparse fault localization under a valid local repair rule
Does not establish general image restoration, learned regeneration, or biological credit assignment

claim: A coherent RGB-only rotatable WorldSplat scene is sufficient evidence that the learned scene geometry is correct.
design: branch-preserved geometry stress test
controls: Failed RGB-only branch retained instead of overwritten
Follow-up Virtual KITTI 2 branch adds metric depth supervision
Separate ray-fix A/B branch preserves the earlier control run
limitations: The main README records this as a qualitative branch-level failure rather than a single scalar benchmark
The result rejects visual coherence as proof of geometry; it does not show that RGB-only scene models are never useful

claim: A maintained recurrent state can be approximately synchronized with fewer full-vector transmissions while preserving most held-out task quality when sender state and readout are held fixed.
design: pre-registered same-task communication tradeoff
controls: Dense sender and event receiver use exactly the same recurrent state and the same linear readout
Registered gate required <=80% of dense transmissions and <=5% relative task-RMSE increase
limitations: Full 8-D correction is still transmitted whenever any component crosses threshold
Local RMS homeostasis is separately mixed and is not established as task-optimal

claim: When publication relevance and input reliability overlap independently, factorized state-repair and publication control can suppress private propagation in cases an exclusive signed router cannot reproduce in one step.
design: held-out overlapping-constraint control

metrics.name: overlap event reduction
metrics.display: 73.3% with unchanged state RMSE and public-event mismatch

controls: Same state-repair decisions in factorized and reset-priority signed policies
Reliability and publication relevance are independent factors that may overlap
Corruption detector threshold selected on training seeds before held-out evaluation
limitations: Synthetic scalar-state world
The result establishes a factorization benefit under overlapping constraints, not a biological interpretation of the intervention sites

claim: Saving octave departures plus the terminal core reconstructs the input to floating-point precision across fixed, changing, nonlinear and noisy purifiers.
design: deterministic purifier-family reconstruction audit

metrics.name: purifier families
metrics.display: own EQ, lattice, five Sigh presets, alternating EQs, rebuilt nonlinear, median and noisy

controls: Purifier trajectory is allowed to change; the identity is tested on the saved states rather than assuming one fixed linear operator
Multiple qualitatively different purifier families use the same additive reconstruction rule
limitations: Exact telescoping proves conservation/bookkeeping, not that the residue coordinates are semantically useful
Full residue stacks are redundant and can be expensive to store

claim: Changing the purifier changes where object-aligned structure appears: the image-affinity operator keeps object layout in the surviving core while pushing interior detail into residues, but its segmentation is not state of the art.
design: pre-registered BSDS500 validation/test benchmark with simple and established segmentation attackers

metrics.name: late-residue object alignment
metrics.comparison: own EQ vs plain lattice; lower means object layout stayed out of late residues

controls: 100-image validation split selects one setting before the 198-image test split
Lab+position k-means baseline
Felzenszwalb-Huttenlocher baseline
Plain lattice, Sigh low-pass and leaky-own-EQ purifier controls
limitations: Low-resolution colour-only affinities do not represent semantic objects
Primary slow-mode segmentation loses to Felzenszwalb-Huttenlocher
The strongest result is where structure lands in core versus residues, not a novel segmentation algorithm

claim: The Sigh residue coordinate transform itself makes latent sources easier for PCA/ICA to recover than raw pixels or matched linear controls.
design: matched three-dimensional PCA bottleneck and NumPy FastICA comparison
controls: Same PCA dimension and same ICA implementation for every representation
Orthogonal redundant coordinates
Random encoder matched to the Sigh encoder singular values
replication: three-seed attacked comparison plus exact frame-geometry receipt
limitations: Synthetic linear source-separation task
Rejects a coordinate-change explanation; it does not reject operator-based grouping

claim: Repeated common motion can write persistent feature-pair compatibility that later binds a stopped object at new coordinates rather than merely memorizing its old location.
design: synthetic common-fate write with shuffled-motion and absolute-coordinate controls
controls: Objects are moved to new coordinates and stopped before readout
Part-shuffled motion attacker
Absolute-coordinate edge-memory attacker
Opposing-motion control collapses learned compatibilities to about 1e-14
limitations: Gate 4 uses oracle motion and discrete appearance types
Establishes a mechanism in a synthetic scene, not natural-image object discovery

claim: Additional temporal memory can predict whether a clean-looking recovery prefix will persist when paired futures have exactly the same observed RGB-derived history.
design: paired counterfactual identical-prefix observability attacker

metrics.name: first post-split RGB observation balanced accuracy

controls: Stable-recovery and relapse futures share the exact same noisy RGB-derived prefix
Raw, cumulative, symmetric and asymmetric state families are all deterministic functions of that prefix
limitations: Synthetic tracking world
The result is an observability boundary for the supplied history, not a statement that relapse is intrinsically unpredictable

claim: A genuinely informative RGB-derived motion-surprise observable can predict pre-relapse risk before ordinary confidence diverges, while the causal meaning of that observable depends on the world's contingency.
design: train/validation/test cue selection followed by frozen-rule contingency-shift panel and scalar recalibration control

sample.unit: held-out paired world per Gate-19 scenario

controls: Ordinary mean confidence is matched between stable and relapse-prone recovery histories
Shuffled selected-cue control
Oracle-motion control matches RGB prediction in Gate 19
Broken-contingency world tests whether recalibration can invent absent information
Reversed-contingency world tests whether a stale mapping becomes actively wrong
replication: 40/30/80 train-validation-test Gate 18 plus five Gate-19 worlds with 80 untouched pairs each
limitations: The worlds deliberately define motion instability as predictive, non-predictive or reversed
Shows a measurement/meaning decomposition and calibration boundary, not universal natural-video causality

claim: A correct relation partition can replace a large fraction of pixel measurements in a world that is piecewise constant on that partition, while spatial and shuffled-relation controls cannot.
design: matched-budget sparse-pixel reconstruction with oracle relation, spatial-lattice and shuffled-relation controls

metrics.name: random true-relation first tested budget at >=90% success

controls: Same sparse pixel budget for relation, spatial-lattice and shuffled-relation reconstructions
Shuffled relation preserves group count/size while destroying alignment with the true object partition
limitations: Gate 0 supplies an oracle relation graph
Piecewise-constant synthetic RGB world
Establishes an upper bound on the value of correct structure, not a learned sensing mechanism

claim: Ordered common-fate history can learn a persistent relation that survives spatial rearrangement and reduces the measurement budget of a future frame to the oracle relation curve.
design: past-motion relation learning followed by future rearrangement and sparse sensing with time-shuffle, coordinate-memory and spatial controls

metrics.name: learned relation first tested budget at >=90% PSNR>=40 dB success
oracle relation first tested budget at >=90% success

controls: All hidden objects use the same multiset of velocity vectors in different temporal orders
Independent temporal shuffle destroys common-fate order while preserving the motion vocabulary
Absolute-coordinate memory is attacked by rearranging parts before the future sensing task
Oracle relation retained as a ceiling
limitations: Patch correspondence across history and future is supplied
Synthetic piecewise-constant patches
Does not yet derive tracking confidence from image evidence

claim: Local correspondence uncertainty can be converted into a local measurement budget that stays near the oracle cost curve, rather than forcing blind trust or global oversampling.
design: train/freeze confidence threshold followed by held-out correspondence-swap panel and shuffled-confidence matched-cost attacker

metrics.name: adaptive mean measurements with 4 wrong matches
oracle mean measurements with 4 wrong matches

controls: Always-trust policy keeps the four-measurement budget and fails once correspondence is wrong
Global-caution policy measures all 16 patches
Shuffled-confidence attacker keeps essentially the same number of low-confidence flags/measurements but assigns them to the wrong patches
Oracle uncertainty provides the minimum-cost ceiling
replication: 80 training worlds for threshold selection; 80 untouched test worlds per ambiguity level
limitations: Confidence is synthetic rather than derived from RGB/matching evidence
Patch identity is still available to the synthetic tracker
The gate establishes the budgeting mechanism, not a real visual tracker

claim: A charged low-resolution image guide can derive correspondence confidence that localizes where expensive sensing is needed, retaining most of the synthetic-confidence budget advantage under cross-object look-alike ambiguity.
design: train/validation/test image-match cue selection with explicit guide sensing cost and matched-cost shuffled-confidence attacker

metrics.name: adaptive total cost with 4 ambiguous guides
adaptive total cost with 6 ambiguous guides

controls: Guide channel cost is included in every adaptive sensing budget
Three image-derived diagnostics are calibrated on training worlds and selected on a separate validation set
Cross-object look-alike blending creates genuine wrong nearest-template correspondences
Shuffled-confidence attacker preserves nearly the same total sensing cost while assigning caution to the wrong patches
Full high-resolution scan is the 100% sensing baseline
replication: 80 train, 40 validation, and 80 untouched test worlds per ambiguity level
limitations: Synthetic guide/content sensor split
Guide images are low-dimensional synthetic appearances rather than natural video
Expensive content is still exactly shared inside each hidden relation in Gate 3

claim: When a learned relation is only approximately predictive, a cheap current residual observable can decide which local members need their own expensive measurement and achieve the same quality-cost curve as an oracle residual policy in the tested sparse-innovation regime.
design: relation-model mismatch with charged low-dimensional projection, trained residual threshold, equal-cost random-extra attacker, and oracle residual ceiling
controls: Fixed one-expensive-read-per-relation baseline
Equal-cost random-extra policy buys exactly the same number of additional expensive reads as the adaptive policy but at random non-anchor locations
Oracle residual policy uses true anchor-copy error to identify exactly which patches require their own read
Full scan is the 100% sensing baseline
Guide projection cost is included in the adaptive and oracle budgets
replication: 100 training, 50 validation, and 80 untouched test worlds per innovation level
limitations: Innovations are sparse and deliberately strong
The cheap projection is synthetic and unusually clean in this regime
Does not yet quantify the trade-off when the measurement operator itself is sparse

claim: Sparsifying each guide measurement reduces coordinate-touch/mixing cost but creates a measurable sample-complexity price because sparse relation failures can fall outside the measurement support; a moderate sparse regime can preserve sensing quality with substantially less mixing work than a dense guide.
design: row-support × guide-row sweep with trained thresholds, separate detector and end-to-end policy validation, then frozen held-out evaluation

sample.unit: held-out world per innovation level for each selected feasible row support

metrics.name: support-1 best tested minimum validation success
support-2 best tested minimum validation success

controls: Innovation modifies only 8 of 192 high-resolution coordinates, so sparse rows can genuinely miss the changed support
For each row support, guide-row count is selected only by a separate end-to-end validation panel before held-out testing
Scalar guide sample count and coordinate-touch/mixing cost are reported separately
Dense support-192 guide provides a same-sample-count comparison for moderate sparse support-64 sensing
replication: 100 training worlds, 50 detector-validation worlds, 40 policy-validation worlds per innovation level, and 80 untouched test worlds per level
limitations: Synthetic sparse innovations and random linear guide measurements
The experiment is an executable analogue of measurement-sparsity trade-offs, not a validation of an asymptotic theorem
Designed sparse sensing is tested; post-hoc sparsification of an originally dense operator remains open

claim: When relation failures are extremely sparse, deliberately designing sparse measurement supports to cover the signal coordinates can preserve the target reconstruction frontier with much less guide mixing work than post-hoc pruning of dense measurement rows.
design: matched sparse-row support budget with guide-row sweep comparing coverage-designed sparse, post-hoc top-weight pruning, independent random sparse and dense sensing; train/freeze thresholds and select smallest validation-passing row count before held-out evaluation

sample.unit: held-out world per innovation level for each selected sensing family

controls: All sparse methods use row support 64 on the same 192-coordinate signal and the same one-coordinate innovation world
Coverage-designed rows maximize union support before repeating coordinates
Post-hoc pruning starts from dense Gaussian rows and keeps only the 64 largest absolute coefficients in each row
Independent random sparse supports provide a same-sparsity no-design control
Dense Gaussian sensing provides a full-support comparison
Each family learns its own threshold and selects the smallest row count only from a separate validation panel
replication: 150 training worlds, 80 validation worlds per innovation level, and 120 untouched test worlds per level
limitations: Innovation support is intentionally one coordinate, making blind-coordinate coverage maximally important
Synthetic relation world and linear guide sensing
Does not imply coverage-designed sparsity will retain the same advantage for diffuse failures or natural signals

claim: Full coordinate coverage is not sufficient for robust sparse relation-failure sensing once an innovation may contain multiple signed coordinates; overlapping measurement diversity is required to prevent cancellation from hiding changed combinations.
design: freeze Gate-6-selected sensing geometries and support-1-trained thresholds, then sweep innovation support from 1 to 64 while approximately holding total innovation energy fixed

sample.unit: held-out world per innovation-support × innovation-patch-count cell

controls: Gate-6 sensor geometries are frozen rather than reselected for each support size
Residual thresholds are trained only on support-1 worlds and frozen
Per-coordinate innovation amplitude scales as 0.65/sqrt(K), approximately holding total innovation energy constant
Coverage-designed sensor continues to touch all 192 signal coordinates, ruling out untouched coordinates as the cause of its support-2 failure
Post-hoc-pruned and random-sparse 12-row sensors provide high-redundancy overlapping-measurement controls
replication: 150 support-1 training worlds and 120 untouched test worlds for each of 7 support sizes × 5 innovation-patch levels
limitations: Synthetic signed innovations and linear sensing
The robust 12-row controls spend four times the coordinate-touch budget of the three-row coverage sensor
The experiment identifies a need for measurement diversity but does not yet find the minimum-cost coded sparse design
